channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Quaest: maioria vê Lula 'amigável' com Trump e reunião boa para o Brasil
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll released today shows that most respondents viewed the meeting between Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and U.S. President Donald Trump, held on Thursday (7), positively. Interviewees described the encounter as friendly and beneficial for Brazil.

item.title: Oposição não vai atrapalhar plano de segurança, diz Wellington Lima
item.description: Justice Minister Wellington Lima stated that the relationship between government and opposition will not interfere with the Brazil Against Organized Crime program, launched by President Lula with an R$ 11 billion investment. He said the initiative aims to ensure security agents fulfill their duties and will not be politicized or influenced by political noise. The program consists of four pillars: financial strangulation, weapons trafficking and circulation, prison system containment, and forensic investigation and crime resolution.

item.title: Indústria: Fiesp e CNI criticam MP que acaba com "taxa das blusinhas"
item.description: Fiesp and CNI criticized the Provisional Measure that ends the 'blusinhas tax', arguing that the exemption of taxes on international purchases up to US$50 creates unfair competition, harms national industry, and benefits foreign producers, especially from China. The entities state that the measure destroys jobs and sabotages the Brazilian economy.

item.title: Desconforto de Lula e Alcolumbre chama atenção em posse no TSE
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senate President Davi Alcolumbre appeared visibly uncomfortable during the inauguration of Kassio Nunes Marques at the TSE, signaling ongoing tension between them following legislative defeats to the government. Their strained relationship worsened after Alcolumbre personally led the defeat of Jorge Messias’ STF nomination and supported overturning Lula’s veto on the Dosimetry Bill. Despite the rift, Lula’s allies believe he will avoid escalating the conflict, hoping for future rapprochement to prevent interference with priority executive proposals in Congress.

item.title: Crusoé: Eleitor não acredita na moderação de Lula e Flávio, aponta Quaest
item.description: Brazilian voters doubt the moderation of Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) ahead of the 2026 presidential election, according to a Genial/Quaest poll. 45% of respondents believe Lula is not more moderate than the PT, while 40% think he is. The survey indicates widespread skepticism about either candidate’s ability to distance themselves from their parties’ ideological bases.

item.title: Fim da taxa das blusinhas opõe varejo nacional e importadores; veja argumentos a favor e contra
item.description: President Lula's administration repealed the 'blusinhas tax,' which imposed a 20% import duty on international online purchases under $50, while keeping the Remessa Conforme compliance program. The move sparked a national debate: domestic retailers and manufacturers argue the tax was needed to level the playing field against foreign e-commerce platforms, while importers and consumers welcome its removal as a reduction in living costs. However, ten Brazilian states continue to apply a 20% ICMS on such purchases, preserving part of the tax burden.

item.title: Trump: o melhor cabo eleitoral de Lula
item.description: The meeting between Lula and Donald Trump contributed to a slight improvement in Lula’s personal and government approval ratings, according to Quaest polling, with a 3 to 4-point recovery over the last two weeks. Lula gained traction across all income and education levels, including traditionally unfavorable groups like evangelicals and voters in the South and Center-West, and tied with Flávio Bolsonaro in the pivotal Southeast region. Approval for the Desenrola 2 policy and the ban on betting for the indebted also boosted his image, outweighing negative news such as the Senate’s rejection of Jorge Messias.

item.title: Para chefão do PT, pesquisas ainda não captaram efeito Trump e Messias
item.description: PT national president Edinho Silva says recent polls have not yet captured the positive effects of Lula’s meeting with Donald Trump and the Senate’s rejection of Jorge Messias’ STF nomination, which Lula’s allies believe will boost him electorally. In the Genial/Quaest poll released this week, Lula stands at 42% and Flávio Bolsonaro at 41% in a second-round simulation, technically tied after Bolsonaro’s son led in April. Edinho Silva notes most voters are not yet focused on the October elections.

item.title: "Não tenho rabo preso", diz Salles em batalha contra Nunes e Centrão. Veja vídeo
item.description: Deputy Ricardo Salles (Novo) rebutted criticisms from São Paulo Mayor Ricardo Nunes (MDB), claiming he 'has no tail tied' and can speak freely, while accusing the Centrão of being 'Brazil's cancer' and allied with the PT. Salles rejected the Centrão's support for André do Prado's Senate bid, stating that Nunes' MDB is a base of Lula's government. Nunes, in turn, accused Salles of narcissism and individualism, saying he only creates confusion and that his electoral success depended solely on Bolsonaro's backing.

item.title: PL cria grupo de trabalho sobre eleições e já tem 2 sugestões ao TSE
item.description: The PL has created a working group to develop suggestions for the 2026 elections, coordinated by Deputy Eduardo Pazuello, with two proposals already ready: decentralizing vote counting to states and removing electoral zones from areas controlled by drug trafficking or militias. The suggestions will be delivered to TSE President Nunes Marques after the group finalizes them.

item.title: Lula reassume vantagem numérica sobre Flávio Bolsonaro no 2º turno, diz Quaest
item.description: Lula regained a numerical lead over Flávio Bolsonaro in the runoff scenario, with 42% to 41%, within the margin of error. His approval rose to 46%, perceptions of the country’s direction improved, and exposure to favorable news rose from 23% to 32%. The president reversed months of decline, gaining ground in approval, voting intention, and national outlook.

item.title: Após culto com Malafaia, Flávio Bolsonaro cresce entre evangélicos e cai entre católicos
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro improved his image among evangelical voters after attending a service with Pastor Silas Malafaia, gaining five points of support compared to April, but lost four points among Catholics. Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva showed the opposite trend: gaining five points among Catholics and losing one among evangelicals in the same period. The event sparked controversy, with a complaint filed to the Federal Public Ministry over alleged premature electoral propaganda.

item.title: Bolsonaro poderá ter a condenação revista por Nunes Marques? Entenda o pedido de revisão criminal no STF
item.description: Minister Kassio Nunes Marques, appointed as rapporteur at the STF, will review the criminal revision request of Jair Bolsonaro's conviction for attempted coup d'état, assessing whether there were procedural nullities in the First Chamber's ruling. The defense argues the sentence contradicted penal law or the evidence in the case files, but did not request precautionary measures. Any potential annulment would only occur after full procedural compliance, possibly culminating in a Plenary vote.

item.title: A posição veemente do varejo nacional ao fim da ‘taxa das blusinhas’
item.description: The federal government's decision to eliminate the 20% import tax on international purchases under US$50, known as the 'blusinhas tax,' triggered immediate backlash from national retail and industry groups, who warn it harms domestic production, worsens tax asymmetry, and threatens small businesses and jobs. Entities such as CNI, IDV, Abvtex, and Abit argue the measure favors foreign platforms—especially Asian ones—in sectors like apparel and electronics, undermining local competitiveness. Conversely, representatives of international platforms and digital commerce advocates claim the revocation boosts purchasing power for low-income families and expands access to consumption.

item.title: Pacheco decide não concorrer em MG, mas ainda terá conversa com Lula
item.description: Senator Rodrigo Pacheco decided not to run for governor of Minas Gerais in 2026, citing an unfavorable electoral scenario for the left in the state. He will still hold a conversation with President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva to attempt to change the situation, but now prioritizes a nomination to the Federal Court of Accounts (TCU). The decision was communicated to PT national president Edinho Silva in a meeting in Brasília.

item.title: Os artistas presentes na posse de Nunes Marques no TSE
item.description: The inauguration of Kassio Nunes Marques as a minister of the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) was followed by a private party in Brasília, featuring performances by artists such as Jorge Aragão, Dudu Nobre, Ivo Meirelles, Sombrinha, Gusttavo Lima, Henrique e Juliano, Raimundo Fagner, and the presence of coach Wanderley Luxemburgo. Nunes Marques even sang the chorus of 'É Hoje' with a microphone during the event. The celebration included VIP areas, a sophisticated menu, and tickets sold for R$ 800, according to backstage reports.

item.title: 'Amanhã você amanhece morto': Briga de deputados expõe racha no PL em Goiás em meio ao afastamento entre lideranças
item.description: The PL directory in Goiás has been plagued by internal rifts since 2024, hindering the formation of a strong majority ticket for the 2026 elections. The distancing between Senator Wilder Morais, pre-candidate for governor, and federal deputy Gustavo Gayer, pre-candidate for Senate, is worsened by a physical altercation in the state legislature between state deputies Major Araújo and Amauri Ribeiro, which ended in a death threat and accusations of betrayal and alignment with the group of former governor Ronaldo Caiado.

item.title: Partido de Denarium tenta usar precedente do Rio para adiar eleição em Roraima
item.description: The Republicans party asked the STF to suspend direct elections in Roraima, which were mandated by the TSE following the removal of Governor Edilson Damião, arguing that the same precedent used to delay the supplementary election in Rio de Janeiro should apply to Roraima. The party requests that the president of the Roraima Legislative Assembly, Soldado Sampaio, remain in office until the STF rules on the succession case in Rio, where Judge Ricardo Couto serves as interim governor. Former Governor Antonio Denarium, a political ally of Sampaio, was also declared ineligible in the same ruling that removed Damião.

item.title: Pesquisa Quaest mostra acerto nas ações do governo para recuperar imagem de Lula, avaliam assessores
item.description: The Quaest poll shows Lula at 42% and Flávio Bolsonaro at 41% in a technical tie for the second round, with presidential advisors crediting government actions for improving Lula’s image. The improvement is linked to the launch of Novo Desenrola Brasil, the meeting with Donald Trump, and the repeal of the 'shirt tax,' particularly boosting support among women and voters earning two to five minimum wages. However, Lula continues to struggle with evangelical voters, while gaining ground among Catholics.

item.title: Fim da ‘taxa das blusinhas’: o que muda nas compras internacionais agora
item.description: The federal government has abolished the so-called 'blusinhas tax', a 20% import duty on international purchases under US$ 50 made via the Remessa Conforme program. The change, enacted through a provisional measure signed by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and a Ministry of Finance ordinance, takes effect on Wednesday, March 13, 2026. While purchases under US$ 50 are now exempt from federal taxes, they remain subject to state ICMS (17-20%), lowering final prices on platforms like Shein, Shopee, and AliExpress; purchases above US$ 50 continue to face a 60% import tax plus ICMS.

item.title: As intenções de voto de Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro entre evangélicos e católicos, segundo a Quaest
item.description: Lula leads among Catholics with 51% voting intention versus 34% for Flávio Bolsonaro, while the senator leads among evangelicals with 61% against 24% for the president. Overall, Lula has 42% and Flávio 41%, maintaining a technical tie but showing a positive trend for the petista since April. The Quaest survey, with a two-point margin of error, was conducted between May 8 and 11 with 2,004 interviews.

item.title: Quaest indica melhora na aprovação de Lula em meio a Desenrola e Trump
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll shows President Lula's approval rose from 43% to 46%, while disapproval fell from 52% to 49%. This improvement comes amid positive news from the launch of Desenrola 2.0 and a mysterious meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump.

item.title: Valdemar Costa Neto diz que vê Nunes Marques mais aberto a voto impresso
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto, national president of the PL, said that Minister Kássio Nunes Marques, the new president of the TSE, is more open to supporting the implementation of printed voting in Brazil. The remarks were made following Nunes Marques' inauguration to the post on Tuesday night, the 12th, in Brasília.

item.title: Festa de Nunes Marques reúne políticos, cantores e apenas dois ministros do STF; veja quem foi
item.description: A party organized by Ajufe in honor of the new TSE president, Kassio Nunes Marques, gathered politicians, sertanejo singers, and only two STF ministers (Gilmar Mendes and André Mendonça), who left the event quickly. With tickets priced at R$ 800, the event featured performances by Gusttavo Lima, Fagner, Jorge Aragão, and others, along with the presence of Attorney General Paulo Gonet and Senate pre-candidate Vanderlei Luxemburgo. Nunes Marques avoided endorsing candidates, stating that Electoral Justice acts indirectly to improve Brazil.

item.title: Fim da taxa das blusinhas: Lula acha que o eleitor é otário
item.description: The 'blusinhas tax', introduced under the guise of tax justice and national industry protection, was repealed just before the 2026 elections after failing to meet revenue targets and creating market distortions. Its short lifespan exemplifies the opportunistic use of economic policies for electoral gain, without delivering promised outcomes. President Lula is criticized for treating voters as naive, announcing the repeal only when the issue became politically inconvenient.

item.title: Entre veto, Congresso e STF: a crise institucional da Lei da Dosimetria
item.description: Congress overturned the presidential veto on the Dosimetry Law, which alters penal rules for those convicted in the January 8 attacks, but the STF suspended its application pending constitutional review. The promulgation included a unilateral 'splitting' of provisions by Congress President Davi Alcolumbre, which lacks explicit constitutional basis, triggering a new institutional crisis among the branches of government.

item.title: O que parlamentares da oposição esperam de Nunes Marques na presidência do TSE
item.description: Minister Nunes Marques assumed the presidency of the TSE after his swearing-in on Tuesday night, the 12th, succeeding Carmen Lucía. Opposition lawmakers expect him to act with impartiality and independence during the 2026 elections, avoiding favoritism toward any party, particularly given his appointment to the STF by Jair Bolsonaro. The expectation is that his leadership will strengthen the credibility of the Electoral Justice in a polarized context.

item.title: Bolsonarismo fica encurralado por derrubada da ‘taxa das blusinhas’ e calcula tema na campanha de Flávio
item.description: The repeal of the 'blusinhas tax' by the Lula government via a Provisional Measure created a tactical dilemma for Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign, which must avoid appearing to support a popular measure while also not seeming contradictory, given that Bolsonarism originally opposed the tax. The adopted strategy is to criticize the government for 'selling out the country' to boost re-election, linking the tax repeal to a broader set of policies — including the PEC to end the 6×1 work scale — to frame it as a desperate attempt to halt Flávio's rise in the polls and avoid backlash.

item.title: Jogos de hoje, quarta, 13 de maio: onde assistir futebol ao vivo e horários
item.description: On Wednesday, May 13, 2026, football fans face a packed global schedule, highlighted by the Coppa Italia final between Lazio and Inter Milan at 16:00, alongside Premier League, LaLiga, Ligue 1 matches and decisive Copa do Brasil second-leg fixtures involving Vasco, São Paulo, Palmeiras and Atlético-MG. The day also features J1 League games, Argentine and Mexican league matches, and Women’s Super League action.

item.title: Novo estrategista de comunicação de Flávio Bolsonaro já foi processado por Lulinha
item.description: Journalist and publicist Alexandre Oltramari, newly hired for Flávio Bolsonaro’s 2026 pre-campaign communications team, was previously sued by Fábio Luís Lula da Silva, known as Lulinha. The lawsuit, not detailed in the excerpt, stems from a prior conflict involving Oltramari. The report is presented as exclusive and requires a subscription for full access.

item.title: Receio eleitoral levou Lula a acabar com taxa das blusinhas
item.description: President Lula abolished the 'blusinhas tax', a 20% federal levy on international purchases under US$50, following polls showing high rejection, especially among lower-income groups. The move, enacted via provisional measure on May 12, 2026, aims to reduce electoral damage ahead of the 2026 elections, as the tax had become a negative symbol of his government and a political asset for the opposition.

item.title: Por que pesquisas eleitorais 'erram'?
item.description: Electoral polls are not designed to predict election outcomes, but to capture voter intention at the time of interviewing. When well-conducted, they neither 'err' nor 'succeed' — they simply provide a 'snapshot of the moment'. Discrepancies between polls and final results stem from voter volatility, campaign events, and statistical margins of error, not inherent methodological flaws.

item.title: Dança das cadeiras efetiva Toffoli no TSE, muda perfil e atrai holofotes do caso Master
item.description: The departure of Minister Cármen Lúcia and the appointment of Kassio Nunes Marques as president of the TSE led to the effective inclusion of Minister Dias Toffoli as a full member of the Electoral Court, solidifying a shift in the tribunal’s profile. This move draws attention due to Toffoli’s connection to the Master case, which involves allegations of corruption and undue influence in elections. The article notes the change will take effect this month and is available only to subscribers.

item.title: Comissão da escala 6 X 1 recebe Boulos e fundador do movimento VAT
item.description: The special committee of the Chamber of Deputies held public hearings to discuss reducing the workweek and ending the 6x1 scale through PEC 221/2019, focusing on impacts on women and small businesses in the morning and social dialogue in the afternoon. Invited guests included Guilherme Boulos, Minister of the Presidency’s General Secretariat, and Rick Azevedo, founder of the VAT (Life Beyond Work) movement, along with union, government, and business representatives.

item.title: Fim da taxa das blusinhas preocupa indústria
item.description: The federal government abolished the import tax on international purchases under US$ 50, known as the 'little shirts tax,' effective May 13, 2026, retaining only the 20% ICMS state tax. The move triggered strong backlash from national industry groups, including CNI, Abit, Abvtex, and the Parliamentary Front in Defense of Intellectual Property, who argue it creates unfair competition for Brazilian firms, threatens jobs, and reduces public revenue.

item.title: Governo Lula quer esperar quadro completo de negociação com Trump antes de fazer ofertas sobre tarifas
item.description: The Lula government has decided to wait for a complete picture of the U.S. trade negotiations before making formal tariff reduction offers on American products, despite a positive meeting between Lula and Trump at the White House. Brazil’s approach is cautious: initial talks will focus on clarifying bilateral trade data, with both sides’ teams having 30 days to advance negotiations, particularly regarding the Section 301 investigation on Pix. Lula demanded detailed updates from his ministers following the meeting, underscoring centralized control over foreign policy.

item.title: Taxa das blusinhas, Desenrola 2.0 e crédito a motoristas de app: governo Lula acelera medidas de olho nas eleições
item.description: The Lula government announced the end of the 'blusinhas tax' (Remessa Conforme) for international purchases up to US$50, aiming to boost popularity ahead of the 2026 elections. It also launched a new Desenrola Brasil program and is preparing credit lines for app-based drivers, while dealing with public weariness over rising household debt and declining Petrobras profits.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro resgata aliados escanteados no governo do pai em equipe de pré-campanha
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro is building his 2026 pre-campaign team with allies who were sidelined during his father's government, such as former Justice Secretary Vicente Santini and digital strategist Marcos Aurélio Carvalho, aiming to decentralize communication control and professionalize the bolsonarist structure. The inclusion of Marcos Cintra, former economist under Paulo Guedes, reinforces the effort to reconstruct a technical and political base less dependent on the family nucleus. This move is interpreted as a strategy to rearticulate bolsonarism ahead of the 2026 presidential election.

item.title: Com resistência de Pacheco, Lula admite dificuldade em Minas e vê PT à deriva no estado
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva acknowledges the difficulty of consolidating Rodrigo Pacheco’s candidacy for governor of Minas Gerais after the senator reiterated his refusal to run, citing personal, family, and health reasons. Although Pacheco said he wants to speak with Lula before making a final decision, the PT is facing political paralysis in the state, with allies delaying regional alliances while waiting for his stance, which has allowed opponents to advance and created a climate of stagnation and demoralization within the party.

item.title: Inteligência artificial, urnas eletrônicas e Ficha Limpa: veja quais serão os principais desafios de Nunes Marques à frente do TSE
item.description: Kássio Nunes Marques assumed the presidency of the TSE and will face challenges including regulating the use of artificial intelligence in electoral campaigns, such as banning AI-generated content 72 hours before elections, defending electronic voting machines against disinformation attacks, and applying a revised interpretation of the Clean Record Law that could allow previously ineligible politicians to run. He will also handle inherited sensitive cases, including cassation requests over social media disinformation involving bolsonarist figures, and oversee the drafting of electoral resolutions for the 2026 elections.

item.title: PL já avalia retirar candidatura de Eduardo Bolsonaro como suplente de chapa ao Senado em caso de condenação no STF
item.description: The PL is already considering removing Eduardo Bolsonaro as Senate substitute candidate if he is convicted by the STF, due to potential ineligibility under the Clean Record Law. The Federal Prosecutor’s Office has concluded its final arguments in a case accusing him of coercion and attempting to interfere in the trial of former President Jair Bolsonaro, seeking conviction for orchestrating international sanctions against Brazil. While his defense invokes parliamentary immunity and free speech, party leaders are preparing for automatic removal from the ballot should he be convicted.

item.title: Defesa das urnas, climão com Alcolumbre, Michelle ao lado da mulher de Moraes: tudo sobre a posse de Nunes Marques no TSE
item.description: Kassio Nunes Marques assumed the presidency of the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) in a ceremony attended by President Lula, Senators Flávio Bolsonaro and Davi Alcolumbre, First Lady Michelle Bolsonaro, and the wife of Minister Alexandre de Moraes. In his speech, Nunes Marques defended the electronic voting system as an institutional heritage of Brazilian democracy and warned about the risks of illegal AI use and the need to protect freedom of expression in the 2026 elections.

item.title: Governo comemora nas redes o fim da taxa das blusinhas
item.description: The federal government celebrated on social media the end of the 'blusinhas tax', which eliminated the 20% import tax on international purchases up to US$50, announced by President Lula on May 12, 2026. The tax had generated R$5 billion in 2025 and R$1.7 billion in the first four months of 2026, but caused political backlash for affecting purchases on platforms like Shein, Shopee, and AliExpress. Although the federal tax was repealed, state-level ICMS still applies to such imports.

item.title: Decisão de 'taxa das blusinhas' foi política e desagradou equipes técnicas que veem prejuízo a comércio
item.description: President Lula revoked the taxation of international purchases up to US$ 50, known as the 'blusinhas tax,' in a political decision that displeased technical teams at the Ministries of Finance and Development, Industry, Commerce and Services, who warn of harm to domestic commerce.

item.title: Dosimetria: o que se sabe sobre a aplicação da lei e os próximos passos no STF
item.description: The STF is reviewing the constitutionality of the Dosimetria Law, which allows sentence reductions for those convicted of anti-democratic acts. Minister Alexandre de Moraes has suspended its application pending judgment, requesting input from the AGU, PGR, Presidency, and Congress. Four actions filed by political parties and the ABI claim the law undermines constitutional principles by trivializing attacks on democracy.

item.title: Gusttavo Lima e Macallan: a festa de Nunes Marques após posse no TSE
item.description: Minister Kassio Nunes Marques celebrated his inauguration as president of the TSE with a lakeside party in Brasília, attended by officials from the three branches of government, politicians such as Flávio Bolsonaro, singer Gusttavo Lima, and performances by Jorge Aragão and Dudu Nobre. Organized by Ajufe, the event featured cigars, Macallan 18-year-old whisky, and raised R$ 640,000 from 800 tickets sold at R$ 800 each.

item.title: VÍDEO: Em festa regada a uísque e charutos, Nunes Marques solta a voz ao lado de Jorge Aragão: 'Vou festejar'
item.description: Minister Nunes Marques, newly appointed president of the TSE, celebrated his inauguration with a lavish party in Brasília featuring whiskey, cigars, and a samba performance, singing alongside Jorge Aragão and other artists. The event gathered judiciary authorities, politicians like Flávio Bolsonaro, and figures from sports and music, with tickets priced at R$800. During the party, he performed classic samba songs and made a symbolic reference to his appointment, drawing applause from the audience.

item.title: Lula acelera medidas: haverá tempo?
item.description: Lula accelerated the rollout of key policies to boost his government's approval and 2026 electoral prospects, launching the new Desenrola, an R$11 billion organized crime plan, and repealing the 'tax on small clothes'. These moves aim to counter mounting pressure amid economic and security challenges.

item.title: Festa de Nunes Marques tem uísque, ministro no palco e ingresso de R$ 800; veja bastidor
item.description: The inauguration party for Kassio Nunes Marques as president of the TSE in Brasília featured an R$ 800 entry fee, Macallan 18 whiskey in the VIP area and Johnnie Walker Black Label on the dance floor. Despite ideological diversity among attendees — including Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) and Orlando Silva (PCdoB-SP) — many guests could not greet the honoree, who spent most of the night in the VIP section. The event included samba performances, STF and STJ ministers, and a clear VIP-advocate divide, sparking discussion about exclusivity.

item.title: O desafio de enfrentar o crime organizado no Brasil - O Assunto #1718
item.description: The federal government launched the 'Brazil Against Organized Crime' program, featuring R$1.06 billion in direct investment and a R$10 billion credit line for states, municipalities, and the Federal District to fund public security actions and equipment. President Lula stated he aims to approve the Public Security PEC this year to create a dedicated ministry. Former National Public Security Secretary Colonel José Vicente Silva Filho analyzed the plan’s potential to deliver results and warned about the politicization of the security agenda.
